question: Organic nitrates relieve angina primarily by which mechanism?

answers.text: Converting to nitric oxide (NO), which activates guanylyl cyclase, increases cGMP, and causes venodilation reducing cardiac preload

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Nitrates are metabolised to NO → cGMP via guanylyl cyclase → smooth muscle relaxation. Venodilation reduces venous return (preload) and wall tension, lowering myocardial oxygen demand. At higher doses, arterial dilation also reduces afterload.

answers.text: Blocking L-type calcium channels in coronary arteries, causing vasodilation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. That is the mechanism of dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (e.g. amlodipine). Nitrates act via the NO–cGMP pathway, not calcium channel blockade.

answers.text: Inhibiting β1-adrenergic receptors to reduce heart rate and myocardial oxygen demand

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Beta-blockers reduce heart rate and contractility by blocking β1 receptors. Nitrates have no direct adrenergic blocking action.

answers.text: Activating KATP channels to hyperpolarise vascular smooth muscle cells

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. KATP channel activation is the mechanism of nicorandil (a potassium channel opener). Nitrates act via NO → cGMP.

overallFeedback.feedback: Nitrates are NO donors → activate guanylyl cyclase → cGMP → vascular smooth muscle relaxation → venodilation (↓preload) is the primary anti-anginal mechanism, reducing wall tension and myocardial O₂ demand.
Well done. The NO → cGMP → PKG → myosin light-chain dephosphorylation cascade is the central mechanism. Preload reduction (venodilation) is the dominant anti-anginal effect at therapeutic doses.
